kernel.scope: Original official vmlinuz static PCI/controller/board initialization continuation; no official code execution, no hardware access.
kernel.finding: PCI enumeration/sorting and selected UGREEN/watchdog initialization do not establish the eight physical M.2 connector maps. ACPI register_slot consumes _ADR/_SUN; an independently identified board BIOS/AML payload and silkscreen correspondence remain required.
static_inference: This kernel supports generic PCI enumeration and optional DMI/boot-option breadth-first sorting; those paths explain an ordering source but cannot turn dynamically allocated NVMe numbers into connector labels.
An ACPI _SUN path is a genuine positive next source, but a firmware-provided slot number is not by itself proven to equal a NAS M.2 silkscreen label. BIOS revision matters.
limits: The current evidence covers the explicitly named PCI/ACPI initialization, all decoded .pci_fixup registrations, selected DMI hooks and confirmed UGREEN string-reference functions. It is not a proof that the entire firmware lacks another board rule.
Indirect helper calls inside every fixup were not recursively decompiled. No complete kernel CFG or all-callgraph coverage is claimed.
No runtime PCI topology, ACPI AML tables from a target BIOS, connector labels, device population changes or cold-boot ordering has been validated.
No prior nvme.ko dynamic-ID proof was repeated. No changes to kernel/driver source or compatibility mappings were made.

native.finding: Actual native InfoServiceImpl HardwareInfo vtable resolves to a generated default/UNIMPLEMENTED method. Native exact model/DMI helpers and 32-entry enum were traced; their revision labels do not establish GT BIOS-to-physical-SATA pairing. The closed default-service path should not be retraced as a hidden slot map.

unknown.GT_BIOS_SATA: No BIOS version/board identity paired to physical SATA order established by this native chain.
unknown.controller_or_physicalslot: No positive native implementation establishing controller registration order to board silk-screen slot order recovered. Generated request/response fields do not establish such mapping.
unknown.hardware_validation: No NAS programs executed; no physical device reads/writes or live validation.

static_inference.claim: Status code 0x0c with empty strings is consistent with the generated gRPC UNIMPLEMENTED default. The vtable and body therefore close this candidate as a slot-map entry point for this shipped native InfoServiceImpl.

Native get_hw_version does not provide evidence for GT BIOS-to-SATA selection: this recovered helper reads product_version/CPU, its model map lacks GT, and no disk operation occurs in the body. Its rev labels must not be equated to the Go storage_serv hardware-revision map.

No direct call or tail-jump to native get_hw_version was found when decoding the shared library .text. It is a real callable implementation, but its runtime reachability via indirect/dynamic calls was not established.

next_positive_entrypoint.native_chain: This concrete native InfoService HardwareInfo chain is closed: default method, no implementation to extend. RegisterRoutes 0xfe0e0 only checks whether a service exists and returns a status; it does not register hidden hardware HTTP handlers.

outside_native_candidate.bounded_question: Trace this already-proven callee implementation only if controller/physical-slot PCI provenance still needs resolving. It is the pcie_bridge_id branch and is bypassed by the eight block_name successes, so it cannot be advertised as closing those eight physical slots without new evidence.

firmware_evidence: Original ugpt is a Makeself shell archive, gzip tar validated against embedded MD5;10 members extracted without execution
Tool.main dispatches the only MCU-specific updater from explicit arch_spu=rk3588; AMD64 follows vmlinuz/initrd branch
That updater names UGREEN_CEC_Controler_APP_* and reads bus4/address0x15/register0x11, then conditionally stages image under/boot
No I2C flash transaction is implemented inside updata_mcu_fireware itself; staging does not prove later consumer behavior
inference: This concrete upgrader branch is a different interface from DH2600/DXP480T N76 at0x31/0x26; it cannot define their output/PWM/timing readback
unknown: Other untraced library or firmware payload paths are not excluded
N76 application firmware/output/PWM/timing readback still unconfirmed

historical_runtime_phase.finding: Original block_name basename comparison and dynamic NVMe instance naming traced; 20 UPKs / 5209 members / 380 bounded text files indexed. Existing native and upgrader follow-up supersedes its open entrypoint list.

bios_safety_phase.finding: Per-operation LED identity checks and optional BIOS diagnostics; GT SATA remains unknown for every BIOS until a positive physical pairing, and unknown SATA blocks shared U.2 LED positioning. Existing administrator calibration remains explicit.
